Help is always available through the Menu Button in the top-left corner.
Build your story by dragging from an entity's output port to a Scene: this both wires the connection and adds the entity to that Scene at once.
There is no global entity state. Change a name, colour, description, or attribute at a Scene and it carries forward to every Scene downstream.
Entities come in five types plus Knowledge: Characters, Locations, Items, Factions, and your own Custom types.
Mark which Character carries the POV at a Scene. The sequence of POV Scenes defines your story's reading order, which can differ from the temporal layout on the canvas.
A Scene with no POV Character is treated as off-screen, and only appears in your export if you opt in to the off-screen appendix.
Give entities custom attributes that are plain text, a value picked from a Preset List, or an uploaded image, audio, or video file.
Preset Lists let you define reusable value sets, like a Gender or Species list, then pick from them on any entity's attributes.
Relationships connect any number of entities, with each participant carrying their own perception of how they see the others.
Faction membership and Location hierarchy both use the relationship system: a Faction's members and a parent Location's contents are tracked the same way.
Give a Character aliases, then track who knows them by which name with the awareness levels Unaware, Nominally aware, Partially aware, or Fully aware.
Awareness tracking answers who knows what: mark which entities are aware or unaware of an entity, attribute, alias, or relationship.
Circumstances and Motivators record what a Character is going through and what is driving them at a given Scene, each with an intensity.
Group Scenes into Chapters and Acts. Coloured header bands across the top of the canvas show the structure at a glance.
Tag your story and entities, then filter the Table of Contents or search to focus on just what matters.
Open the Text Editor on the right to write a Scene's prose with rich formatting, and turn on name highlighting to see entity mentions in their own colours.
Use Find and Replace in the Text Editor to make changes in this Scene or across all Scenes at once.
The Timeline Navigator lays out your Scenes as columns and entities as rows, with a dot in each Scene where an entity appears or changes.
Pin a Scene's time of day, weekday, date, season, and duration to keep your story's chronology straight.
Export your story to Word, PDF, HTML, Markdown, or plain text, choosing a preset such as NarrativeNode native, Shunn manuscript, or a NovelCrafter-ready bundle.
Build a project quickly by pasting a populated story template, which can bring in entities, scenes, relationships, and your chapter and act structure all at once.
Watch the Alerts panel for an orphaned entity with no incoming wire, or a downstream change that may need review after you edit something upstream.
